name: production-kernel-head-dim-coverage

head_dims.summary: Across seven production attention kernels (verified against source on 2026-09-06), D={64,128} is the universal core; 96 is widely second-class (instantiated in FA2/FA3, padded in vLLM-Triton/SageAttention); 256 is natively instantiated in FA2/FA3/FlashInfer/llama.cpp-mma but has the thinnest Turing story; 512/576 exist only for MLA (FlashInfer DISPATCH includes 512; llama.cpp 512/576 DKQ with 512 DV; vLLM FA4 hd512 selection issue #53175). Odd LLM dims (80, 112, 320) are covered only by llama.cpp and FlashInfer-mixed (192,128).
head_dims.flashattention2: Instantiated set on current master: {32, 64, 96, 128, 192, 256} (csrc/flash_attn/src/flash_fwd_hdim*_sm80.cu and flash_fwd_launch_template.h define exactly run_mda_fwd_hdim{32,64,96,128,192,256}). Historical note: v2.7.4 also instantiated hdim160 (set was {32,64,96,128,160,192,256}); hdim160 was dropped on the road to 2.8.x. API hard cap: head_size <= 256.
head_dims.flashattention3: hopper/ on main (FA3.x) instantiates hdim {64, 96, 128, 192, 256} in hopper/instantiations/flash_{fwd,bwd}_hdim*_{bf16,fp16}[_softcap]_{sm80,sm90}.cu. Asymmetric QK/V pairs are restricted (only the (192,128) family beyond equal dims, Hopper only). Max headdim error string uses compile-time max_headdim (=256).
head_dims.flashinfer: CUDA-level DISPATCH_HEAD_DIM in include/flashinfer/utils.cuh accepts exactly {64, 128, 256, 512} and FLASHINFER_ERRORs 'Unsupported head_dim' otherwise; vLLM's FlashInfer backend mirrors this as get_supported_head_sizes() -> [64, 128, 256, 512] (citing utils.cuh#L157). FA3-prefill path additionally gates to {64,128,256} plus the mixed pair (192,128) via is_fa3_prefill_head_dim_supported. Head dims above 256 are reachable only through per-stage JIT wrappers, not the plan-run monolithic API.
head_dims.vllm_triton: No head-dim whitelist at all: backend gate is `supports_head_size(cls, head_size): return head_size >= 32` (vllm/v1/attention/backends/triton_attn.py), and the launcher pads with headdim_padded = next_power_of_2(self.headdim). So effective set = any head_size >= 32 up to shared-memory limits; Triton JIT-compiles per (padded) dim.
head_dims.cutlass_fmha_xformers: kMaxK-templated dispatch, not per-dim instantiation: explicit sm75 and sm80 kernels exist for kMaxK = 64 (64x64 register-fragment), 128 (32x128 rf), and 65536 (32x128 gmem-accumulation single-iteration variant) for f16/f32 (bf16 only on sm80); kernels with head_dim > kMaxK are skipped at dispatch (pytorch aten attention.cu: `if (value.size(3) > Kernel::kMaxK || key.size(3) > Kernel::kMaxK) return false`). Practical coverage: <=64 via 64x64, <=128 via 32x128, larger dims only through the gmem variant when the whole KV fits one block iteration.
head_dims.llama_cpp_fattn: Three sub-paths with different sets. MMA (tensor-core) path switch on Q head dim: {64, 80, 96, 112, 128, 256} with V==K, plus asymmetric combos 192/128 (MiMo-V2.5, gqa%8), 320/256 (Mistral Small 4, gqa%32), 512/512, 576/512 (DeepSeek; GLM 4.7 Flash gqa_ratio=20 special-cased); anything else hits `GGML_ABORT("fatal error")` in the dispatch but is filtered earlier by selection. Tile (no tensor core) path instance list today: dkq{40,64,72,80,96,112,128}+dv same, 192/128, 256/256, 320/256, 512/512, 576/512 (template-instances/fattn-tile-instance-*.cu). Vec (small-batch) path: {64, 128, 256} only.
head_dims.sageattention: CUDA kernels (SageAttention2/2++): DISPATCH_HEAD_DIM accepts only {64, 128} (csrc/dispatch_utils.h), throwing 'Unsupported head dim' otherwise. The sageattn() wrapper zero-pads head_dim<64 up to 64 and 64<head_dim<128 up to 128 (q, k, v all padded), and raises ValueError 'Unsupported head_dim' above 128; 96 therefore runs via padding to 128. SageAttention1 (Triton, sageattention-1 branch) natively supported {64, 96, 128} and announced 48/72/256.

qkv_dim_divergence.flashattention2: Not supported: single head_size for q/k/v/out; padding via kvcache path pads all of q/k/v identically to a multiple of 8.
qkv_dim_divergence.flashattention3: Supported with restrictions: head_size_v may differ from head_size only on Hopper (TORCH_CHECK(dprops->major == 9, 'Only Hopper supports different V headdim')); the allowed family beyond equal dims is head_size in (128,192] with head_size_v in (96,128] - i.e. the MLA-like (192,128) pair.
qkv_dim_divergence.flashinfer: First-class: plan-run API takes head_dim_qk and head_dim_vo separately (ValueError when either > 256 on the monolithic kernel); is_fa3_prefill_head_dim_supported explicitly whitelists (192,128); MLA kernels cover 576/512 (kv_lora_rank+rope = 576 cached).
qkv_dim_divergence.vllm_triton: Supported: the V1 AttentionSpec carries head_size and head_size_v separately, and a dedicated TritonAttentionDiffKVBackend exists alongside FlashAttentionDiffKVBackend for qk_dim != v_dim models.
qkv_dim_divergence.cutlass_fmha_xformers: Partially: kernel tracks head_dim and head_dim_value separately (dispatch checks both against kMaxK); PyTorch/xformers mem-efficient path historically required them equal in wrappers but the CUTLASS kernel itself models d_qk and d_v independently.
qkv_dim_divergence.llama_cpp_fattn: Supported for exactly three asymmetric combos, each added for a named model family: 192/128 (MiMo-V2.5), 320/256 (Mistral Small 4), 576/512 (DeepSeek/GLM); selection returns BEST_FATTN_KERNEL_NONE (fallback) if K/V dims do not match the combo constraints.
qkv_dim_divergence.sageattention: Not supported: q, k, v are padded to the same rounded head_dim; no qk!=v kernel.

kv_heads_gqa.flashattention2: GQA supported via num_heads/num_heads_k division check (TORCH_CHECK num_heads % num_heads_k == 0) and PackGQA kernel option.
kv_heads_gqa.flashattention3: Same divisibility check; PackGQA built into sm90 kernels; llama.cpp-style gqa-ratio-specialized tiles do not exist here.
kv_heads_gqa.flashinfer: GQA group size is a template dispatch axis: DISPATCH_GQA_GROUP_SIZE accepts {1,2,3,4,6,8}; larger ratios fall back to non-templated handling.
kv_heads_gqa.vllm_triton: GQA handled by kernel grid mapping over kv heads; no ratio whitelist observed in the backend gate.
kv_heads_gqa.cutlass_fmha_xformers: GQA via num_heads_q % num_heads_kv in wrapper checks; no head-count instantiation.
kv_heads_gqa.llama_cpp_fattn: GQA ratio is a first-class specialization axis: ncols2 (KV columns per Q tile) is chosen from gqa_ratio (%2/%4/%8/%16/%32), with per-cc tables (e.g. 576/512 on Turing picks ncols2 16/32 depending on KV length; the 320/256 path requires gqa_ratio % 32 == 0).
kv_heads_gqa.sageattention: Group-query attention supported (README 2024-11-11 note); no ratio-specific instantiation.

hybrid_pattern.summary: Out of this item's core scope; the only hybrid-relevant evidence found is llama.cpp's MiMo-V2.5 comment in fattn.cu (gqa_ratio 8 for SWA layers vs 16 for full-attention layers sharing the 192/128 head shape, i.e. the same kernel must serve both layer kinds), and vLLM #38918/#52433 where Gemma-4's per-layer mixed attention (sliding-window locals + large-dim globals) forces mixed attention backends. No linear-attention/GDN coverage was researched here.
hybrid_pattern.uncertain_marker: [uncertain] hybrid-layer pattern handling inside each kernel was not independently verified beyond these two data points.

heterogeneous_dims.summary: Per-layer head-dim divergence within one model is the 2025-2026 stress case. Evidence: (1) vLLM #38918 '[Usage]: Gemma4 on Turing GPUs (SM 7.5): all attention backends hit shared memory limits' (open as of 2026-09-06) - heterogeneous Gemma-4 leaves no working backend on Turing; (2) vLLM #52433 (Gemma-4 E4B with mixed attention backends) and #53175 (Gemma4 FP8 KV FA4 head dim 512 backend selection) show vLLM now resolves heterogeneity by per-layer backend mixing rather than one kernel; (3) llama.cpp answered the same pressure by adding asymmetric DKQ/DV instantiations (192/128, 320/256, 576/512) into a single dispatch; (4) vLLM added dedicated *_diffkv backends (FlashAttentionDiffKVBackend, TritonAttentionDiffKVBackend).
heterogeneous_dims.anchor_check: The brief's anchor 'vLLM #40094 forces TRITON_ATTN for heterogeneous head dims' does NOT match: vllm-project/vllm #40094 (2026-09) is '[Bug]: Turbo Quant keep failing TRITON_ATTN kv_cache_dtype not supported' (L4/sm89, open). No PR/issue with that exact claim was found; flag as unverified anchor.

supported_dims.flashattention2: Mechanism: explicit per-hdim template instantiation generated by csrc/flash_attn/src/generate_kernels.py; HEADDIM_SWITCH dispatches to run_mha_fwd_hdim{32,64,96,128,192,256} (hdim160 dropped after v2.7.4 which still had {32,64,96,128,160,192,256}). API layer: head_size<=256 hard error 'FlashAttention forward only supports head dimension at most 256'; head_size%8==0 required; internal round_multiple(head_size, head_size<=128?32:64) with build-time TORCH_CHECK(d==d_rounded) 'This flash attention build does not support headdim not being a multiple of 32' for the non-kvcache path.
supported_dims.flashattention3: Mechanism: explicit instantiations hopper/instantiations/*_hdim{64,96,128,192,256}_[softcap_]sm{80,90}.cu; API: 'FlashAttention forward only supports head dimension at most ' + std::to_string(max_headdim); head_size%8==0 (alignment) checked; asymmetric V dim only on Hopper. vLLM gates its FA3 usage to {64,128,256}+(192,128) regardless of the wider FA3 set.
supported_dims.flashinfer: Mechanism: hybrid - CUDA DISPATCH_HEAD_DIM whitelist {64,128,256,512} plus JIT compilation for new instantiations; (512,512) FA2 entry was added in #3576 and later removed from the default AOT wheel (+~326 MB wheel size, commit 54a6156), so 512 is JIT-only in released wheels. Plan-run monolithic API raises ValueError for head_dim_qk>256 or head_dim_vo>256; per-stage wrappers unlock >256.
supported_dims.vllm_triton: Mechanism: generic autotune + next_power_of_2 padding - no instantiation list; supports_head_size head_size>=32 is the only gate (verified verbatim in triton_attn.py). Backend-level alternative gates in the same tree: FlashInfer backend get_supported_head_sizes()=[64,128,256,512]; b12x [64,128,192,256]; hpc_attn [128]; base AttentionBackend returns [] (unconstrained).
supported_dims.cutlass_fmha_xformers: Mechanism: kMaxK template ceiling - kernels instantiated for cutlass::arch::Sm75 and Sm80 with (kQueriesPerBlock, kKeysPerBlock, kMaxK) = (64,64,64), (32,128,128), (32,128,65536); the 65536 gmem variant removes the head-dim ceiling only for single-iteration (short-KV) cases. As of xformers v0.0.33+ the python op 'cutlassF-pt' delegates to aten::_efficient_attention_forward (kernel upstreamed to PyTorch); docstring: 'GPUs as old as P100 (Sm60)'.
supported_dims.llama_cpp_fattn: Mechanism: explicit DKQ/DV switch statements plus precompiled template-instance .cu files (template-instances/fattn-tile-instance-dkq{40,64,72,80,96,112,128,192,256,320,512,576}-dv*.cu) to bound compile time. Historical quote verified verbatim at commit f3f65429c4 (2024-06-26), fattn-tile-f16.cu line 290: GGML_ASSERT(false && "FlashAttention without tensor cores only supports head sizes 64 and 128."); the tile path has since been widened (e.g. PR #15769 'CUDA: faster tile FA (Pascal/AMD), headsize 256', 2025-09) so today only the vec path is still restricted to {64,128,256}.
supported_dims.sageattention: Mechanism: strict template whitelist {64,128} in CUDA DISPATCH_HEAD_DIM + host-side zero padding for dims between (0,128) and hard error above 128; SageAttention1 Triton kernels natively {64,96,128}; sageattention-1 README (verified): 'Support for head_dim values of 64, 96, and 128 is currently available. Extended support for values 48, 72, and 256 will be available soon.' - 48/72/256 remain unshipped in CUDA kernels as of 2026-09-06 (issue #166 'head-dim lower than 128' and #204 'plans to support qk_head_dim = 192 in DeepSeek MLA' both open).

capability_gate.flashattention2: Floor: compute capability >= 8.0 (README requirement #1: 'Ampere, Ada, or Hopper GPUs ... For Turing GPUs (T4, RTX 2080), see the separate flash-attention-turing repo (ssiu/flash-attention-turing), which supports a core subset of FlashAttention features on Turing'). Runtime dispatch keys on is_sm80/is_sm8x/is_sm90 (flash_attn_interface.py). Real blockers on Turing: cp.async (Ampere-only instruction used throughout FA2 mainloop) and no mma.sync 16x8x16 fp16 pipe tuned path; the official answer is a fork, not a fallback.
capability_gate.flashattention3: Primary gate: Hopper sm90 WGMMA/TMA; current main additionally compiles sm80 kernels (flash_fwd_kernel_sm80.h, enable_sm80_to_sm89, mainloop_fwd_sm80.hpp) so FA3.x now covers sm80/89 for standard dims. FP8 requires sm89/sm90. Asymmetric V headdim requires dprops->major == 9.
capability_gate.flashinfer: README (as quoted by maintainer in #1648): 'FlashInfer currently provides support for NVIDIA SM architectures 80 and higher and beta support for 103, 110, 120, and 121.' SM75 is de-facto partially compatible but unowned: maintainer (yzh119) in #1648: 'We have a subset of kernels that are compatible with SM75, the only issue is test coverage (we don't have a SM75 CI machine so some of changes we made to the kernels might break SM75)'. vLLM raises its FlashInfer floor to SM80 because 'FlashInfer supports SM75+, but is currently broken on SM75 (Turing)' (issue #3620, fix PR #3621) - the floor stays at DeviceCapability(8,0) until that fix lands.
capability_gate.vllm_triton: No kernel-level arch gate in the Triton backend itself (Triton JIT targets whatever PTX the driver accepts, so sm75 works, subject to shared memory); gates live in FA utils instead: FA4 on Blackwell (major>=10) rejects head_size>128 except (256,256) and (192,128) 'due to TMEM capacity limits, defaulting to FA version 2'; FA3 unavailable on Blackwell (downgrade to FA4/FA2); FA version selection downgrades with warnings rather than errors.
capability_gate.cutlass_fmha_xformers: Explicit sm75 instantiation is the whole point: _uses_tensorcores(sm, is_half) returns True for sm>=80 always, and for sm>=70 when dtype is half - i.e. Turing uses fp16 tensor cores, older cards and fp32 fall back to SIMT math. Kernel dispatch keys directly on cutlass::arch::Sm75 vs Sm80 types. This is the only mainstream production kernel with first-class Turing tensor-core attention.
capability_gate.llama_cpp_fattn: MMA path gated by turing_mma_available(cc) (sm75+); Volta has a separate volta_mma_available branch; AMD MFMA/WMMA branches; no-tensor-core devices fall to the tile kernel. Turing receives extra special-casing inside the dispatch: `(GGML_CUDA_CC_IS_NVIDIA(cc) && ggml_cuda_highest_compiled_arch(cc) == GGML_CUDA_CC_TURING)` forces the ncols2=32 build for small batches, and the 576/512 case has a dedicated cc>=GGML_CUDA_CC_TURING branch choosing ncols2 by KV length (16384 threshold).
capability_gate.sageattention: Hard floor sm80: core.py sageattn switch handles arch in {sm80, sm86, sm89, sm90, sm120, sm121} and raises ValueError(f'Unsupported CUDA architecture: {arch}') otherwise - Turing (sm75) is not in the switch. CUDA INT8+FP8 kernels need Ampere-class INT8 mma and sm89/sm90 FP8; sm75 survives only through SageAttention1's Triton kernels (issue #197: RTX 2060 'Solved using sageatt 1 and triton 3.1').

fallback_semantics.flashattention2: Hard error: TORCH_CHECK raises Python RuntimeError for head_size>256 ('only supports head dimension at most 256') and for non-multiple-of-8; there is no silent slow kernel. The only automatic padding is the kv-cache path, which zero-pads q/k/v to the next multiple of 8 and slices the output back. On Turing the package simply cannot run (no sm75 kernels compiled) - users must switch kernels; no eager/degrade path.
fallback_semantics.flashattention3: Hard error at API boundary (TORCH_CHECK with max_headdim message; 'Only Hopper supports different V headdim'; 'Deterministic backward not supported for hdim 256'). Callers implement their own downgrade: FlashInfer's determine_attention_backend silently returns 'fa2' when is_fa3_prefill_head_dim_supported fails; vLLM logs warning_once and downgrades FA version (e.g. 'FA4 on Blackwell does not support head_size=%d due to TMEM capacity limits, defaulting to FA version 2.').
fallback_semantics.flashinfer: Layered: CUDA level FLASHINFER_ERROR ('Unsupported head_dim'); python plan-run level ValueError for >256 on monolithic kernels; backend-determination level silent fallback (unsupported FA3 dims -> 'fa2'). Downstream (vLLM) the backend is deselected via get_supported_head_sizes before launch, so unsupported dims never reach the kernel.
fallback_semantics.vllm_triton: Most permissive: head_size>=32 accepted and padded to next_power_of_2, so unsupported-dim fallbacks surface only as resource failures (vLLM #38918: on Turing, Gemma-4's large dims make ALL backends hit shared-memory limits - an error, not a slow path) or as kernel-side incompatibility bugs (#40094: TRITON_ATTN 'kv_cache_dtype not supported'). FA paths degrade with logged warnings to FA2; FA2-with-hd512 needs FA4 (flash_attn backend supports_head_size: <=256 generally, <=512 if FA4 available).
fallback_semantics.cutlass_fmha_xformers: Skip-and-fall-through: dispatch skips kernels where head_dim > kMaxK; xformers operator dispatch (memory_efficient_attention) tries flash -> cutlass -> triton_splitk/math in order and raises NotImplementedError with the accumulated per-operator 'reasons' list when nothing supports the shape; PyTorch SDPA falls through to the math backend (silent slow path).
fallback_semantics.llama_cpp_fattn: Graceful op-level fallback: ggml_cuda_get_best_fattn_kernel returns BEST_FATTN_KERNEL_NONE for unsupported dims/combos, ggml_cuda_flash_attn_ext_supported() returns false, and the ggml-backend scheduler runs the fallback (non-FlashAttention) implementation instead - no crash, no silent wrong kernel. GGML_ABORT('fatal error') exists only as an internal consistency trap inside the dispatch after selection already validated the dim.
fallback_semantics.sageattention: Explicit pad-or-throw: <64 padded to 64, 64<d<128 padded to 128 (silent, zero-pad, changes numerics slightly through smoothing/quant statistics), >128 ValueError 'Unsupported head_dim'; unsupported arch ValueError 'Unsupported CUDA architecture'. No slow fallback provided - the caller must catch and choose another kernel.

ci_hardware_coverage.flashinfer: No SM75 CI, by maintainer admission in #1648 (2025): 'we don't have a SM75 CI machine so some of changes we made to the kernels might break SM75, but if user report related bugs we are happy to fix them.' SM80+ is the supported/CI'd floor; the SM75 breakage (#3620) that vLLM worked around by raising the floor to SM80 is direct evidence that untested-SM75 rot is real.
ci_hardware_coverage.llama_cpp: Split: GitHub-hosted CUDA CI (build-cuda-ubuntu.yml, nvidia/cuda:12.6.2 container) is compile-only with -DCMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES including 89-real - no Turing execution; a self-hosted [Linux, NVIDIA] runner runs real GPU tests (GG_BUILD_CUDA=1 ci/run.sh in build-self-hosted.yml) but is a modern-arch card, not Turing. Turing/Pascal correctness is therefore maintained through community 'Eval bug' reports - e.g. #24400 'Eval bug: Gemma4 E4B crashes with --flash-attn on' on a GTX 1080 (Pascal) with FA + drafter + KV quant (closed as fixed) - plus deliberate Pascal/Turing perf work (PR #15769).
ci_hardware_coverage.flashattention2_and_3: Dao-AILab CI compiles on CPU runners; correctness/perf validation happens on maintainer GPUs (Ampere/Hopper). No Turing execution anywhere in the project; Turing is explicitly delegated to the ssiu/flash-attention-turing fork.
ci_hardware_coverage.vllm: Backend gates are exercised on CI GPUs (Ampere/Ada/Hopper/Blackwell-class); Turing is not in vLLM's CI fleet - evidenced by #38918 (Gemma4 on SM 7.5, all backends hit shared memory limits) being a user-reported usage issue rather than a CI failure. Claims of sm75 support that have visibly rotted elsewhere: FlashInfer #3620 (broken on SM75 despite README saying SM75+).
ci_hardware_coverage.cutlass_fmha_xformers: The sm75 instantiations live in PyTorch's CI'd codebase (aten mem_eff_attention), so they at least compile in every pytorch build; functional GPU CI runs on V100/A100-class runners, not T4 - sm75 correctness relies largely on the huge community of T4 users, not CI.
ci_hardware_coverage.sageattention: No meaningful GPU CI; validation is manual on 4090/3090/A100/H100/5090-class cards per README history. Turing only via the SageAttention1 Triton path (issue #197).
ci_hardware_coverage.uncertain_marker: [uncertain] exact GPU models of llama.cpp's self-hosted NVIDIA runner and xformers/FA maintainer GPU CI are inferred from workflow files and public discussion, not confirmed by vendor documentation.

turing_baseline.summary: No same-hardware (T4/2080Ti/RTX 6000-class) measured attention-kernel numbers were collected in this item; this field documents Turing evidence pointers instead of perf tables. The strongest signals: llama.cpp PR #15769 (2025-09) specifically accelerates the tile-FA kernel for Pascal/AMD and adds headsize 256 - i.e. ggml actively optimizes the no-tensor-core path that Turing-without-mma shares; llama.cpp fattn.cu contains purpose-written Turing branches (ncols2 selection, KV-length thresholds for 576/512); FlashInfer #1648 argues 'Tesla T4 and the RTX 20xx series are still the most common GPUs in the market'; vLLM #38918 documents that on Turing, d256-class Gemma-4 hits shared-memory limits in every vLLM backend; SageAttention #197 shows RTX 2060 working only via SageAttention1 Triton.
turing_baseline.uncertain_marker: [uncertain] no quantified T4/2080Ti kernel benchmark (us or TOPS) was verified in this pass; defer to turing-d256-perf-structure item.

d256_feasibility.flashattention2: Achievable on sm80: hdim256 instantiated; launch template picks 128x64 vs 64x64 block shape based on `max_smem_per_block >= 2 * Headdim * (128 + 2 * 64)` (=~128 KiB request), i.e. d=256 is exactly the smem-budget boundary that Ampere's 164 KiB satisfies and Turing's 64 KiB does not. Backward at d=256 cannot be deterministic. On sm75: absent (cc gate), and the smem equation alone rules it out.
d256_feasibility.flashattention3: Achievable on sm90 (hdim256 instantiated, WGMMA) and now sm80; FP8 hdim256 paths exist; deterministic backward excluded at 256. No sm75.
d256_feasibility.flashinfer: Achievable sm80+: DISPATCH includes 256 (and 512 via JIT); monolithic plan-run API caps at 256 and per-stage wrappers unlock 512; (512,512) wheel-size incident (#3576, +326 MB AOT) shows the AOT cost curve of high-dim instantiation.
d256_feasibility.vllm_triton: Feasible in principle (any head_size >= 32, next_power_of_2 pad), but bounded by shared memory: on sm75 (64-96 KiB smem/SM) a d=256 fp16 KV tile stage does not fit with sane block shapes - empirically confirmed by #38918 where Gemma-4's 256-dim layers exhaust shared memory on every backend including Triton on Turing.
d256_feasibility.cutlass_fmha_xformers: Not for sustained d=256 on Turing: rf kernels cap at kMaxK=128; the kMaxK=65536 gmem variant only covers single-block-iteration (short-KV) cases, which excludes LLM prefill/decode KV lengths.
d256_feasibility.llama_cpp_fattn: Achievable on Turing: the MMA path instantiates DKQ=DV=256 with Turing-specific ncols2=32 scheduling, and the tile path adds dkq256-dv256 (PR #15769) - ggml is the existence proof that d=256 runs on sm75-class hardware by chunking DKQ across smem stages with fp16 accumulators; 576/512 MLA also runs on Turing behind a KV-length-tuned branch.
d256_feasibility.sageattention: Not achievable: >128 raises ValueError; 256 was announced (sageattention-1 README) but never shipped; no sm75 support at all.

cost_analysis.instantiation_cost: Explicit instantiation scales binary/compile cost roughly linearly in supported dims x dtypes x causal/dropout/split variants: FA2 master generates 6 hdims x 2 dtypes x (plain/causal) x (fwd/bwd/split/split_align) files; FA3 splits hopper/instantiations into separate .cu per hdim x dtype x softcap x arch to parallelize nvcc; llama.cpp moved fattn tile/mma instances into template-instances/*.cu for the same reason; flashinfer AOT wheel grew ~326 MB from the single (512,512) FA2 entry before it was pruned (commit 54a6156) - the canonical quantified datapoint that high-dim instantiation is expensive to ship.
cost_analysis.padding_cost: Padding is cheap but not free: vLLM Triton pads headdim to next_power_of_2 (96 -> 128: +33% K-loop work, zeroed lanes); SageAttention pads 96->128 (same overhead) and <64->64; FA2 rounds d to multiples of 32/64 internally and requires it at build time for the non-kvcache path; llama.cpp tile pads DKQ/DV to multiples of 2*warp_size in smem (DVp/DKq) with explicit OOB checks only in the ncols2==1 branch.
cost_analysis.chunking_cost: llama.cpp tile kernel processes DKQ in nbatch_K chunks per KQ iteration (e.g. nbatch_K=64 for d<=128, per-arch tables) and DV via nbatch_V - the register/smem budget mechanism that lets d=256/320/576 run on 64 KiB-smem Turing; FA2's smem-gated 128x64-vs-64x64 tile switch at hdim256 is the same tradeoff at the tile-shape level; xformers' kMaxK=65536 gmem-accumulation kernel trades register accumulation for gmem traffic, usable only when KV fits one iteration.
cost_analysis.uncertain_marker: [uncertain] exact per-dim register/smem budgets for the llama.cpp Turing mma tables (turing_lab would need to compile-and-inspect); only structural mechanisms verified from source.

route.summary: This item informs all three bridge routes. Route A (native d=256 template on sm75): llama.cpp's MMA 256/256 and tile dkq256-dv256 instances prove sm75 d=256 is buildable, with Turing-specific ncols2 scheduling as the key trick; Route B (k-chunked 256 on a 128 pipeline): llama.cpp tile's nbatch_K chunking and xformers' kMaxK-ceiling + gmem-overflow pattern are the two reference mechanisms; Route C (bridge-header completeness for unmodified FA2/FlashInfer): FA2's instantiation set {32,64,96,128,192,256} and FlashInfer's DISPATCH {64,128,256,512} define exactly which dims a bridge must claim to substitute for them, and FlashInfer's SM75 'subset compatible, zero CI' status (#1648, #3620) is the gap a bridge could own.

recommendation.summary: For the sm_75 bridge kernel plan: (1) target the llama.cpp-proven Turing set as the v1 contract - native {64, 80, 96, 112, 128} plus 256 via chunked KQ accumulation (Route B on a 128-wide pipeline), since 96/112-class dims and 256 are the actual production asks (MiMo 192/128, Gemma-4 256, MLA 576/512 only if MLA demand materializes); (2) copy llama.cpp's fallback semantics - report the op as unsupported and let the scheduler fall back (never GGML_ABORT, never silent wrong output), and copy vLLM-Triton's next_power_of_2 padding only for in-range dims; (3) avoid the vLLM #38918 outcome (all backends fail on Turing for Gemma-4) by publishing a per-dim smem feasibility table and declining unsupported dims up front; (4) if substituting FA2/FlashInfer headers (Route C), claim exactly {64,128,256} first - that covers FA2's Turing-relevant instantiation list excluding its Ampere-only extremes, matches FlashInfer's plan-run cap, and leaves 512/576 to a later MLA-specific milestone; (5) set up one T4/2080Ti runner early - every rot story found here (FlashInfer #3620, llama.cpp #24400, vLLM #38918) traces to absent sm75 CI.

numerics_risks.flashattention2: Zero-padding of head dims changes accumulation length (round to 32/64); bf16 unavailable on Turing (README: 'bf16 requires Ampere, Ada, or Hopper GPUs'), so any Turing bridge consumes fp16 with fp32 accumulate; deterministic backward impossible at hdim256 (documented in FA3, inherited design pressure).
numerics_risks.llama_cpp: Documented overflow mitigation in the tile kernel: without v_dot2_f32_f16 there is 'a higher risk of numerical overflow in the KQ calculation', so Q is pre-scaled by 0.25 and KQ re-scaled after - relevant because Turing mma f16 paths share the fp16-accumulate risk profile; softcap compiled only for DV in {128,256,512}; ALiBi (max_bias) forces ncols2=1 paths, narrowing the fast set further.
numerics_risks.sageattention: Quantization-specific: per-block/warp INT8 QK with smoothing, FP8 PV uses two-level accumulation (fp32+fp16 / fp32+fp32) to bound error; padding 96->128 perturbs per-channel quant statistics (zero channels included in max/abs statistics); issue #386 documents int32 overflow silently corrupting Triton outputs for non-contiguous long sequences; #392 documents silently-wrong output on sm120 CUDA-graph replay - the project has a pattern of silent-wrongness bugs, so a bridge reusing its accumulation scheme needs the two-level accumulator.
numerics_risks.flashinfer: Padding-free but per-dim dispatch means numerics differ per instantiation; >256 JIT paths are less-tested (512 removed from AOT after correctness/size churn in #3576).
numerics_risks.vllm_triton: next_power_of_2 padding inserts zero lanes into softmax denominators safely (masked) but widens mma tiles (96->128 perf+numerics-neutral for fp32 accumulate); FA4 Blackwell TMEM limit shows even hardware accumulators bound d.
numerics_risks.uncertain_marker: [uncertain] no independent d=256 accumulation-order study was done in this item; kahan/two-level accumulator necessity at d=256 on fp16 pipelines is inferred from the llama.cpp overflow comment and SageAttention2 paper design.

demand_weighting.summary: Who benefits from widening head-dim coverage on Turing: (1) installed base - FlashInfer #1648: 'Tesla T4 and the RTX 20xx series are still the most common GPUs in the market, covering the widest market share' (T4 is the archetypal cloud inference spare-part); (2) model distribution - 2025-2026 flagship shapes keep stressing non-128 dims: DeepSeek/GLM MLA 576/512 (llama.cpp dedicated Turing branch), MiMo-V2.5 192/128, Mistral Small 4 320/256, Gemma-4 per-layer 256-class locals/globals (vLLM #38918/#52433/#53175), Qwen-style 96/128 mainstream; (3) framework coverage - on Turing today only llama.cpp (tile+mma), xformers/PyTorch cutlass (<=128), and vLLM Triton (generic, smem-limited) deliver; FA2/FA3/FlashInfer/SageAttention all gate sm75 out, so a bridge owning {64..128, 256} has no production competitor except llama.cpp's.
demand_weighting.anchor_note: llama.cpp is the only project observed shipping model-specific asymmetric instantiations (192/128 MiMo, 320/256 Mistral Small 4, 576/512 DeepSeek + GLM 4.7 Flash gqa_ratio=20), a direct read on where demand is pulling.
